speaker_listener_roles_and_relationship.careWorkerToPersonReceivingCare: Warm adult professional speech. Worker uses ako/ko and respectful kayo/ninyo with po/opo; no assumed family bond. Person receiving care uses natural ako and kayo/ninyo to the worker, without manufactured deference or childlike speech.
speaker_listener_roles_and_relationship.peerColleagues: Natural ako/ko and ikaw/mo; neutral respectful requests, with name when needed. Kishimoto and the learner are peers in week01.
speaker_listener_roles_and_relationship.supervisorsMedicalProfessionalsFamily: Use known name or professional/family role with polite kayo/ninyo and po when speaking directly. Do not infer rank, gender, age or family relationship. Distinguish nars, doktor, other professional and care-worker responsibilities.

address_forms_and_conditions.default: Use respectful kayo/ninyo/po for the person receiving care. Do not substitute Lola/Lolo, Nanay/Tatay, Ate/Kuya or gendered titles without source support.
address_forms_and_conditions.requestedAddress: Respect the exact requested surname or given name. Retain Haruko-san, Morikawa-chan and Haruko-chan when the Japanese suffix itself is the learning distinction; no equivalence with a Filipino kinship role.
address_forms_and_conditions.reuse: Preserve the same speaker-listener forms across repeated contexts and subsequent weeks unless the source changes the relationship or states an individual preference.

names_honorifics_and_unknown_gender_age.names: Romanize Tanaka, Haruko Morikawa, Kenichi Hasebe, Fumi Onodera and Misaki Kishimoto consistently. Preserve -san in narrated/address teaching contexts. Speaker labels use names, without invented Mr/Ms or family titles.
names_honorifics_and_unknown_gender_age.unknownFacts: Do not infer gender or age from names. Anak na babae is used only where the Japanese explicitly says 娘. Respect the request for surname without changing it to given name.

register_and_social_phrases.prose: Complete connected adult teaching prose, with explicit actors and conditions. Use direct instructional verbs and a warm respectful tone, avoiding clipped notes or excessive literalness.
register_and_social_phrases.introductions: Render よろしくお願いします as Ikinagagalak ko po kayong makilala in the first-meeting context. It is not a fixed phrase for all uses.
register_and_social_phrases.permission: Maaari po ba… for concrete permission; distinguish consent to the task from consent to moving possessions or sharing information.
register_and_social_phrases.thanksAndAcknowledgment: Use Salamat, Sige po, Opo or an appropriate contextual acknowledgment, preserving whether the source is asking, agreeing or merely confirming.
register_and_social_phrases.refusal: Keep refusal scoped to its object and time; declining photography does not mean declining participation.

preferred_terminology_by_concept_id.glossaryPolicy: Identical Japanese glossary paragraph strings reuse identical whole Filipino target strings, including the Japanese learning label and reading. Contextual inflection is permitted in prose without redefining the shared concept.

headings_punctuation_and_script_fonts.headings: Natural sentence-style Filipino headings; stable recurring lesson headings. Preserve Japanese vocabulary labels and readings as learning material.
headings_punctuation_and_script_fonts.punctuation: Standard Filipino Latin-script punctuation; curly quotation marks for quoted speech, colon for speaker labels. Preserve the teaching-scene label and paragraph boundaries.
headings_punctuation_and_script_fonts.fonts: Use existing approved Royal Latin-script font and fallback. No UI/font/color edits made by this translator.
